articles.title: 4 Ways a Shell Variable Slipped Past Claude Code's Permission Checks
articles.excerpt: Book: LLM Observability Pocket Guide Also by me: Thinking in Go (2-book series) — Complete Guide to Go Programming + Hexagonal Architecture in Go My project: Hermes IDE | GitHub — an IDE for developer…
articles.body: Book: LLM Observability Pocket Guide Also by me: Thinking in Go (2-book series) — Complete Guide to Go Programming + Hexagonal Architecture in Go My project: Hermes IDE | GitHub — an IDE for developers who ship with Claude Code and other AI coding tools Me: xgabriel.com | GitHub Your settings file says "deny": ["Bash(rm *)"] . You read that as "the agent can't run rm". Claude Code reads it as "a command whose text matches rm * doesn't run". Those are two different promises, and the gap between them is the shell. Between October 3 and October 9 , Claude Code 's official CHANGELOG fixed four cases where a shell variable got past a permission check. In two, a deny or ask rule missed the command.

articles.title: ColumnCheck: Local CSV Review with Human Overrides
articles.excerpt: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 2: Side Hustle. ColumnCheck is a small command-line review aid for freelancers handling messy CSV imports. It learns likely col…
articles.body: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 2: Side Hustle . What I Built ColumnCheck is a small command-line review aid for freelancers handling messy CSV imports. It learns likely column meanings from headers, then applies explicit validators for email syntax, ISO calendar dates, decimal amounts, and nonnegative whole-number quantities. It produces JSON and offline HTML reports without modifying the source CSV or sending data to a hosted AI service. The intended customer is someone reviewing invoice exports before importing them into another system. This is a business hypothesis, not evidence of paid demand. There are no customer purchases or validated time-saving claims.

articles.title: Kubernetes Token Rotation Doesn't Revoke Anything. Here's How to Fix That With Bound Marker Secrets
articles.excerpt: You rotate a Kubernetes service account token. The new one works. You update the consumer, close the ticket, and feel good. Then someone asks: "Is the old token dead?" It isn't. A token minted through…
articles.body: You rotate a Kubernetes service account token. The new one works. You update the consumer, close the ticket, and feel good. Then someone asks: "Is the old token dead?" It isn't. A token minted through the TokenRequest API stays valid until its exp claim, whether that is in one hour or in seven days. "Rotation" that only creates a new credential is key issuance . The leak window you were trying to close is still open. This post explains the API feature that makes revocation possible, the extra machinery you need around it, and what we measured when we built it into zenxPAM, Zenxsys's agentless, just-in-time privileged access platform.

articles.title: The Pixel 11 Pro’s 120x zoom is ridiculous, but is it actually useful?
articles.excerpt: The Pixel 11 Pro's extreme zoom is surprisingly useful, but its AI-enhanced images come with some glaring caveats.
articles.body: Google has never been shy about pushing smartphone cameras to their limits. In fact, some might say, eking out the maximum using software instead of hardware is Google’s entire shtick with the Pixel lineup. With the Pixel 11 Pro , the company is taking things even further, quite literally, with 120x Pro Res zoom. That’s a step up from 100x on the Pixel 10 Pro and a ridiculous amount of magnification for a phone. Google claims its brighter telephoto camera can capture more detail from farther away – when combined with generative AI, of course. But just because a phone can zoom in that far doesn’t mean the results will be any good. My previous experience with such bold claims has often fallen flat. So, I was curious to see if Google could do any better.

articles.title: Geospatial Traceability: Connecting Farm Mapping, Satellite Intelligence, and Supply Chains
articles.excerpt: Imagine a container of natural rubber leaving Kochi for a tyre factory in Europe. The paperwork is spotless. Every purchase is recorded, every bale is weighed, every transfer is signed. Now imagine th…
articles.body: Imagine a container of natural rubber leaving Kochi for a tyre factory in Europe. The paperwork is spotless. Every purchase is recorded, every bale is weighed, every transfer is signed. Now imagine three ways it can still be wrong: The farm polygon behind one of those purchases sits 15 metres from the real farm, because the boundary was walked with a phone under a thick canopy. The polygon is right, but a satellite flagged a clearing there in 2022, and nobody knows whether that was forest being cut or an old rubber block being replanted. Both of those are fine, but at the processing plant the rubber was blended with material from a plot nobody has checked. None of these failures shows up if you look at only one system. The transaction ledger looks complete. The map looks precise.

articles.title: I Built ReTrace to Help Generator Technicians Remember Every Repair
articles.excerpt: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 2: Side Hustle I built ReTrace, a voice-first repair-history assistant for independent generator repair technicians. In Nigeria…
articles.body: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 2: Side Hustle What I Built I built ReTrace , a voice-first repair-history assistant for independent generator repair technicians. In Nigeria, many households and businesses rely on generators when public electricity is unavailable. When a generator develops another problem, technicians may have to rely on memory, old notebooks, WhatsApp messages, or scattered notes to remember what was repaired previously. This can lead to repeated troubleshooting and replacing parts without having the full repair history available. ReTrace gives technicians a place to keep that history. A technician can create a customer and generator profile, record a voice note after a repair, and let AI turn it into a structured repair record.

articles.title: Surviving the Solo Ride: Practical Habits for Indie Developers
articles.excerpt: Why the Indie Path Feels Different When you work on a project by yourself, every decision lands on your shoulders. There is no team to share the load, no manager to set deadlines, and often no budget…
articles.body: Why the Indie Path Feels Different When you work on a project by yourself, every decision lands on your shoulders. There is no team to share the load, no manager to set deadlines, and often no budget to cushion mistakes. That freedom is exhilarating, but it also creates a hidden risk: the project can expand faster than your energy or resources allow. The first step to staying afloat is to treat your solo venture like a small business, even if the product never leaves your garage. Set a Fixed Working Rhythm One of the biggest traps for indie makers is the lack of a regular schedule. Without a clock‑in time, it's easy to let work bleed into evenings and weekends, eroding personal time. I experimented with three simple patterns: Time‑box your day - Pick a start and end hour and stick to it.

articles.title: I’ve been a smart home user for 10 years, and the Apple HomeView looks like a game-changer
articles.excerpt: From intrusive ads to clunky software, the smart home landscape has a lot of room to improve. The HomeView could help.
articles.body: Smart displays are a category that, to me, have always felt like they’re on the cusp of being the next big thing for the smart home. I was excited when I first got my Nest Hub . The idea that I could control connected devices with a tap, without having to shout commands at a speaker or pull out my phone, was incredibly appealing. Want to turn off the lights? Just tap a button. Simple, practical. Fast forward to today, and it’s hard not to feel like the category has gone nowhere. Google’s Nest Hub displays are getting long in the tooth, while Amazon’s Echo Show lineup has become increasingly difficult to recommend when so much of the screen real estate is effectively used as a digital billboard.

articles.title: Before Dark Souls, FromSoftware’s Forgotten PS1 Horror Game Was a Haunting Exercise in Empathy
articles.excerpt: FromSoft’s Echo Night asks players to bring peace to the dead.
articles.body: To trace FromSoftware’s history is to uncover a lineage written in cold sweat. While the studio is celebrated today for unforgiving action RPGs like Dark Souls and Elden Ring , its DNA is deeply rooted in games that feel born of a fever dream. FromSoft’s darker legacy lives in games like Kuon , a masterclass in Japanese folklore and survival horror, and Shadow Tower , a claustrophobic dungeon crawler that turns every dark alcove into a deadly trap. Even Eternal Ring — not to be confused with its blockbuster sibling Elden Ring — radiates that signature, unsettling aura that makes exploring FromSoftware’s later worlds so intoxicating.

articles.excerpt: From the Costa del Sol to whitewashed mountain villages, here are 10 of the best places in southern Spain to experience the Aug. 2, 2027 total solar eclipse.
articles.body: Spain is one of the easiest places in the world to experience the total solar eclipse on Aug. 2, 2027 . The so-called "eclipse of the century" first makes landfall in Andalucía, where totality will last up to 4 minutes and 40 seconds during mid-morning, with the sun comfortably high at around 38-42 degrees above the horizon in the eastern sky. Excellent roads, plentiful accommodation and Málaga's international airport make this an obvious alternative to North Africa and the Middle East. However, choosing where to watch requires some thought.

articles.title: 'Let's all choose to make tomorrow better', Artemis II astronauts honored with Stephen Hawking Medal at Starmus
articles.excerpt: The Artemis II crew have joined an impressive list of honourees, including Buzz Aldrin, Jane Goodall and David Attenborough.
articles.body: TENERIFE, CANARY ISLANDS — The Artemis II astronauts may have traveled hundreds of thousands of miles away from Earth to the moon, but they made sure the rest of us didn't miss out on the adventure. Now, their efforts to bring the wonders of space exploration back down to Earth have earned them one of science communication's most prestigious honors: the Stephen Hawking Medal. NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman and Victor Glover , alongside Canadian Space Agency astronaut Jeremy Hansen , accepted the award on Saturday (Oct. 17), during the opening ceremony of the Starmus VIII festival. The honor recognizes all four crew members, including NASA astronaut Christina Koch , who wasn't in attendance.

articles.body: I got my hands on the Google Pixel 11 Pro XL when it launched globally in August, and I’ve spent quite a bit of time with it since. It’s not my daily driver, but I’ve used it enough to know what I love about it and, more importantly, where I wish Google had done things differently. If there’s one thing I’ve come to appreciate about Pixel phones over the years, it’s how Google gets so many of the little things right. From the design and software to how everything feels in everyday use, using a Pixel has a certain charm that’s hard to ignore. Of course, that doesn’t mean everything is perfect. Performance is still one area where I’d love to see Google step things up, especially when you look at what the competition has to offer.

To me, that’s the difference between a brilliant Charlie Brown quote and brilliant Charles Schulz quote, if that makes sense.

articles.excerpt: On Oct. 17, 2016, the Antares rocket now built by Northrop Grumman Space Systems returned to flight to come back from a catastrophic explosion. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Oct. 17, 2016, Orbital ATK (now Northrop Grumman Space Systems ) returned to flight, successfully launching a cargo shipment to the International Space Station (ISS) after its previous cargo mission failed to launch. The private spaceflight company was contracted by NASA to fly cargo to the ISS, and stakes were high for this launch. Orbital ATK's last attempt nearly two years earlier ended in a catastrophic explosion a few seconds after liftoff. Despite some delays, the newly upgraded Antares rocket flawlessly blasted off into the night sky from NASA's Wallops Flight Facility in Virginia. Six days later, the Cygnus cargo spacecraft arrived at the ISS to deliver food, supplies and science experiments to the crew.

articles.body: On Episode 232 of This Week In Space , Rod Pyle and Tariq Malik are joined by Chelsea Gohd, former writer for NASA/JPL and now with Space.com, to talk about the recent large data dump from the Artemis II mission. What was included? Why is this new data important? What observations were made, and what discoveries might result from them? What kind of annotations and notes did the astronauts include that make these observations uniquely valuable? And finally, we talk about Artemis III - what is the mission profile and what are the stakes for SpaceX and Blue Origin? Download or subscribe to this show at: https://twit.tv/shows/this-week-in-space .

articles.title: 6 scientifically accurate star projectors to turn any room into a home planetarium

articles.body: Want to educate young children about the wonders of the cosmos? Depending on the time of year, your location and the weather, your hopes to see the night sky in real life might not be as easy as heading into the backyard and peering up. That's why one of the best star projectors might be the solution. That's why we've picked out six star projectors that actually deliver scientifically accurate images, from projections of the northern hemisphere to breathtaking pictures from the Hubble Space Telescope . Any one of these will turn your home into a private planetarium. Each comes with several swappable images, and you can purchase additional slides/discs for the Homestar and Pococo models.

articles.title: Websites are closing their doors to AI agents
articles.excerpt: Autonomous agents are the hottest thing in AI. OpenAI, Meta, Google, Instinct, and others promise their agents can scour the internet on your behalf, doing anything from booking a dinner reservation a…
articles.body: Autonomous agents are the hottest thing in AI. OpenAI, Meta, Google, Instinct, and others promise their agents can scour the internet on your behalf, doing anything from booking a dinner reservation and cleaning out your inbox to buying new shoes. But what happens when the rest of the internet won't play nice? In recent weeks, users of services like Meta's Muse, xAI's Grok, OpenAI's Dots, and Instinct have reported blocks preventing their AI agents from performing tasks across top websites. articles.title: OpenAI models hacked a crypto wallet and breached more websites
articles.excerpt: The actions could have resulted in criminal charges had humans been behind the keyboard.
articles.body: OpenAI said internal models hacked two more websites, bypassed company-imposed browsing restrictions, and used exposed credentials to draw cryptocurrency from a wallet it couldn’t otherwise access, in the latest installment of disclosures of its agents performing unethical and likely illegal acts. The company on Thursday issued reports of four new incidents, all of which occurred in June. They come after the company revealed in July that internal test agents exploited a zero-day vulnerability in a tool designed to restrict their access to the Internet. They then broke into the network of AI tool provider Hugging Face. The agents took that illegal action to steal answers to a hacking test that weren’t available when completing the tasks on their own.
